evidence.quote: This section summarizes the method from (cite: GB+05) used to study gravitational torques exerted by the stellar potential on the gas distribution and estimate the location of CR.

analysis_steps.goal: azimuthally average torques and identify CR

method.value: Gas-weighted azimuthal average tau(R); CR taken as the negative-to-positive crossing with the largest amplitude within 0.75-2.25 R_bar

evidence.quote: This often results in multiple zero crossings, and we identify the most significant crossing as the one with the largest amplitude, which we associate with $R_{\rm CR}$.
Therefore, we establish $0.75R_{\rm bar}-2.25R_{\rm bar}$ as the range in which we search for the CR of the primary bar.
This is done by an integration of pixels in an annulus defined as $[R+\delta R]$, where $\delta R = 1.5 \ \rm arcsec$.

analysis_steps.goal: derive pattern speed and Lindblad resonances

method.value: Omega_p from the angular velocity curve at R_CR; ILR/OLR from intersections of Omega -/+ kappa/2 with Omega_p using CO rotation curves

evidence.quote: we estimate the pattern speed $\Omega_p$ as the intersection of the position of the $R_{\rm CR}$ and the angular velocity curve, since $\Omega = v / R$
the intersection of $\Omega\pm \kappa/2$ with the pattern speed $\Omega_p$ provides the location of the ILR and OLR, respectively
